chunks: From him, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:
Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام was asked about a man who led a people in prayer while he was without wudu (ablution). He said: There is no repetition upon them, but he himself must repeat.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام, the source of the ruling in this hadith
key_terms.أَمَّ: led the people as Imam in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.قَوْمًا: a group of people praying behind the Imam
key_terms.يُعِيدَ: that he must repeat the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: If an Imam leads salat (prayer) without wudu (ablution), do the people praying behind him have to repeat their prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning congregational salat (prayer) led by an Imam who lacked wudu (ablution). It states that the followers do not have to repeat their salat (prayer), while the one who led them must himself repeat it.
